edges.description: Colonizing bacteria that escape mucosal containment enter the bloodstream.
Encapsulated Hib uses its PRP capsule to resist phagocytic and opsonic-complement clearance.
Bacteria that survive the bloodstream interact with the blood-CSF and blood-brain barriers before entering the cerebrospinal-fluid compartment.
Sustained invasive bacteremia produces systemic fever.
Capsule-supported bacteremia lets invasive H. influenzae persist long enough to reach neurovascular barriers.
Once bacteria seed cerebrospinal fluid, bacterial lipooligosaccharide elicits the local cytokine cascade that drives purulent meningitis.
Early CSF cytokine release precedes and drives the neutrophilic inflammatory influx.
Leukocyte influx and cytokines amplify permeability injury at the blood-brain barrier.
Acute meningeal illness produces poor feeding in infants.
Cortical irritation from meningeal inflammation produces seizures.
Meningeal inflammation can produce a subdural effusion.
Inflammatory injury to the cochlear nerve produces sensorineural hearing loss.
Barrier breakdown and impaired CSF dynamics produce hydrocephalus.
Cortical and subcortical injury produces focal motor deficits.
Neonatal and infant brain injury produces neurodevelopmental delay as a long-term sequela.
The infant-rat hematogenous model measures albumin leakage into cerebrospinal fluid during H. influenzae type b meningitis.
edges.limitations: The model uses infant rats and experimentally delivered bacteria, so it does not recapitulate natural human nasopharyngeal acquisition.

nodes.description: Anti-inflammatory corticosteroid given before or with antibiotics to reduce cytokine-driven neurologic injury, with the clearest hearing-loss reduction signal in Haemophilus influenzae meningitis.

evidence.reference_title: Corticosteroids for acute bacterial meningitis.
evidence.snippet: Corticosteroids were associated with lower rates of severe hearing loss (RR 0.67, 95% CI 0.51 to 0.88), any hearing loss (RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.64 to 0.89) and neurological sequelae (RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.69 to 1.00).

evidence.reference_title: Corticosteroids for acute bacterial meningitis.
